name: Abdul Alhazred
summary: The mad Arab, author of the Necronomicon — in which, according to the deathless Chinamen, there are double meanings the initiated might read as they choose — also remembered as 'the mad poet' who dreamed of the nameless city the night before composing his unexplainable couplet on death and eternity.
description:
Abdul Alhazred is called the mad Arab. The deathless Chinamen said that there were double meanings in his Necronomicon which the initiated might read as they chose.

He enters the record only at second hand, through what the deathless Chinamen were said to have told Castro of the cult's lore.

He is also remembered as 'the mad poet' who dreamed of the nameless city the night before he sang the couplet: 'That is not dead which can eternal lie, / And with strange eons, even death may die' — words later babbled deliriously by a terrified explorer fleeing the city's depths.
